steps.text: In a medium saucepan, combine sugar, flour and salt over a medium heat; gradually stir in milk. Cook and stir over medium heat until the mixture is thick and bubbly. Reduce heat to low and cook 2 minutes more. Remove the pan from heat.
Place a strainer over a clean mixing bowl; set aside.

Beat the egg yolks slightly. Gradually pour 1 cup of the hot custard mixture into yolks, whisking constantly. Return the egg mixture to the saucepan and bring the entire mixture to a gentle boil. Cook and stir 2 minutes before removing the pan from heat. Immediately pour custard through the strainer.
Stir butter, vanilla, and coconut into the hot mixture. Pour the hot filling into the baked pie crust. Cool and refrigerate until set, about 4 hours.

review.reviewBody:
Coconut pie is my husbands favorite and I have used many different recipes over the years and have learned a few tips over the years that help cut down on the amount of time you spend standing over the stove. When I make any custard style pie, I use a stainless steel mixing bowl that will serve as a double boiler, that will fit over a large saucepan, like an 8 quart pan. Use just enough water so the the bottom of the mixing bowl is not touching the water. Bring water to a boil. Using a microwave safe 1 qt measuring cup, heat milk until scaled (tiny bubbles around rim of cup). Be careful not to let milk boil. Add sugar, flour and salt to the stainless steel mixing bowl stir to combine, set bowl over boiling water, add the hot milk and stir with a whisk until smooth. It only takes a few minutes for the mixture to thicken and then you can follow the remainging part of the recipe.
You must be careful as the hot steam will escape for the sides of the bowl and you can get burnt if you are not careful. Use a pot holder or dish towel to hold on the mixing bowl while you stir it. Since using this method, I've never burnt or scorched any filling that I was making and cooking time has been cut in half.

Coconut cream pie is by father's favorite pie and this is the second time I have used this recipe. I selected this recipe because it makes a bigger pie and I like to use a deeper pie plate. My family (& especially my dad!) just love it. I used whole milk and the filling is so creamy - really delish! I increased the coconut to one & a half cups and felt it had plenty of coconut taste. I used the 4 egg whites to make a meringue topping, sprinkled coconut over the top and browned it in the oven. It looked great and tasted better. Thanks Mary!

Turned out Excellent! I took a few of the suggestions from other people such as use 1/4 c of each of cornstarch and flour versus 1/2 cup flour, I heated 2 cups of the milk in the microwave to help it warm quicker, and I put 1 1/2 c of coconut in. I also cooked in a double boiler to keep it from scorching. It thickened really nice, but did not come to a boil.

Great basic recipe! I read through the reviews, good and bad, to make these changes: I heated the milk in the microwave first to speed up the cooking time, I used the double broiler method to prevent scorching, and I added a teaspoon of coconut flavoring along with the vanilla. Also, I used unsweetened coconut flakes- the shredded kind, not the big flakes. Turned out delicious!!!

My other half said this was the best coconut cream pie he's ever had. I used 1 c. coconut milk, 1/2 c. whip cream, 1/2 c. skim and 1 c. whole milk (wanted to use what was left in the fridge), and added 1.5 +/- cups of shredded coconut and the rest was exactly like the recipe. I used a non-stick pan over med (3) gas heat, and stirred, stirred, stirred. And NO BURN! Also, topped it with a pint of heavy whip cream, sweetened with Splenda and a touch of vanilla. This was my first time making this type of pie and it was PERFECT!!!! Not too sweet, very coconutty, and exceptionally delicious. Thanks for the new recipe. It s a keeper!!

This is a very good recipe, but personally I am a huge fan of coconut. So to amp up the coconut flavor a little I added 1 tsp of coconut flavor to the custard. Also the custard didn't turn out as creamy or rich as I'd like it to be so I think next time I will be using cream instead of regular milk. Either that or I will use evaporated. I also used a star tip for icing and dotted the top of the pie with whipped cream and sprinkled on some toasted coconut just for looks.

I have to give this five stars, instead of a baked pie shell, I made a crushed vanilla wafer one; with this crust, it's a four. I should have put forth the extra effort. The custard was yummy, with a velvety texture. I like Trader Joe's shredded coconut; it has a bit of body to it... I will definitely make this again; as soon as I get my pie crust recipe lesson from my friend, Louise. I used coconut cream & the remainder skim milk; also used cornstarch instead of flour. Perfect!

I made the pie yesterday for Thanksgiving. The pie looked perfect and tasted great. I did use a bagged flaked natural coconut that was not sweetened. I toasted some coconut on a cookie sheet in the oven to top it. I did not have a problem with the custard burning. I mixed the ingredients with a whisk at first then switched to a spatula to keep the custard from sticking to the edges and bottom of the pan. The pie was excellent and the only thing I would do differently would be to save the egg whites and make a meringue topping as a previous reviewer did. And plan on making it again tomorrow, it was so good.

I will agree with others in that the directions are vague and had me a little confused. I interpreted them the best I could since I've not sucessfully made a coconut cream pie before and prayed. Turned out great and set up nicely! I placed the dry ingredients in my pre-heated sauce pan and slowly poured the 3 cups of milk in, frequently whisking until it thickened and began to bubble....took awhile. I skipped straining as my custard was smooth and far too thick to go through any strainer I have. I wish the recipe had included a merengue or some other type of topping, so be sure to find a good topping recipe prior to making this. We love coconut so took others advice and added 1.5 cups of coconut and topped the merengue in toasted coconut as well.

This is a great recipe, however, I do make one adjustment. I use coconut milk in place of milk for a great coconut taste. I top it with whipped topping mixed with sour cream with a touch of sugar added. Gives it a slight tang instead of just sweetness.
I used a 15 oz can of Trader Joe's Coconut milk, and the rest just milk. Used 3 Tbsp corn starch instead of flour. Added 2 1/2 cups coconut. Perfect! Was a big hit at the party
It makes 2 pies and yes it’s set to the x1 directons. Too much flour and bland. Worst thing I ever made from all recipes

I’ve made this for my FIL twice now. It’s his favorite pie! I use coconut extract instead of vanilla which gives it a delicious extra coconut flavor. This is my go to base recipe for all cream pies because it’s easy and turns out great every time
My family loves this pie. Easy to follow directions.
Well, I haven't made a coconut cream pie in years. And this is as much like mom's recipe that it was easy to follow and taste great!!
This is so so good for coconut lovers. The coconut isn’t too strong with 1 cup, which I appreciated. I would recommend adding a meringue to the top for sure, then bake the flakes for the top.
Just like the one my Grandma made!
This is an amazing recipe!!! AMAZING !!!! Everone one loved it.
